(plan the-suite-is-green-at-head, section s2; reviewed node grace-baseline-reuses-the-timestamp-parser)
reviewed_base_sha: 825bf5bc8d9fb4b1f269ec8712392eda0085a8ef
reviewed_head_sha: 4a6747c600bf16e91e21772b6315cb6748a658ad

The change is product code: reckon/crew/dispatch.py:8501 _iso_stamp_to_ns now reads the grace
supervisor's attempt-start stamp through reckon._timestamps.parse_utc instead of a direct
datetime.fromisoformat call, keeping its None-on-unreadable return. The commit is 4a6747c, whose
parent is exactly the recorded base 825bf5bc8 (git rev-parse 4a6747c^). The diff is 2 insertions and
5 deletions, no other file touched.

Semantics: parse_utc routes a string through parse_iso (which strips surrounding whitespace and
turns a trailing Z into +00:00), reads a naive value as UTC, and returns None for a malformed one.
For the reachable input set this reproduces the removed body exactly except that padded whitespace
is now accepted rather than returning None (a strict widening), and a non-str numeric input now
resolves to an epoch rather than returning None. The sole caller, dispatch.py:8535, always passes a
str (it wraps the source in str(...) first), so the numeric widening is unreachable in-tree; it is
recorded below as a follow-on docstring/contract note, not a behavioural regression.

The guard test tests/test_dispatch_timestamps_reuse_the_parser.py::test_only_the_lane_reading_retains_fromisoformat
(scoped to module dispatch by importlib) asserts the only function in dispatch.py enclosing a
fromisoformat call is _lane_reading_carry; it was red at base because _iso_stamp_to_ns still carried
the second call, and green at head. I read the reviewed worktree at head 4a6747c and never wrote it
(git status clean), and I re-ran the gate myself from a scratch copy of that tree.
